answer: The nadir graph is rebuilt each epoch, as a result the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the vine audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 99 keys loses far more than 99 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the voyage checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 16 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
